executive_assessment.text: Named lowland farming areas face documented flood and drought impacts; Podgorica and coastal areas have dated fire and heat observations.
The plan warns of possible competition over water among agricultural, public-supply and tourism users; no violence is established.
Gender, disability, remoteness and municipal information gaps can limit response. National plans and social assistance arrangements are capacities, not demonstrated adaptation outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: The 2025 adaptation plan identifies projected longer dry periods and reduced agricultural water availability in the Zeta and Bjelopavlici plains and coastal areas, warning that pressure on water supply could produce water-use conflicts, especially involving tourism.
Source dated 2025-06 reports: Lowlands around Zeta, Bjelopavlici, Bojana and Lim have experienced flood damage to crops and infrastructure.
Source dated 2025-06 reports: A 2022 hailstorm damaged vineyards and orchards in Zeta Plain; Plantaze estimated losses at €8 million.
Source dated 2024-10 reports: The 2011 drought affected Zeta and Bjelopavlici; 2017-2018 drought lowered Morača and Zeta river and Skadar Lake levels, harming farming, fisheries and power generation.
Source dated 2023 reports: The report says most 2022 wildfires occurred along the coast and in Podgorica municipality; Montenegro was largely spared in 2023.
Source dated 2023 reports: In August 2023, Podgorica recorded its first 24-hour period with temperatures never below 30°C since records began.
Source dated 2023 reports: Dry months in 2022 reduced hydropower and nearly all power relied on the Pljevlja coal plant, a major air-pollution source.
Source dated 2023 reports: January 2023 heavy rain triggered landslides and damaged roads and bridges in Pljevlja, Mojkovac and Rožaje; a person died in Herceg Novi.

known_gaps.text: No primary source reviewed established that armed conflict, organized violence or insecurity disrupts climate adaptation in Montenegro; the NAP's water-use conflict statement is conditional and not an observed violence record.
The 2020 Drought Plan's institutional status and group statistics are historical and should not be treated as current 2026 conditions.
The World Bank's Annex C has a figure heading referring to Serbian municipalities despite being in Montenegro's country compendium; that table was excluded from claims pending clarification.
The proposed 2025 national extreme-weather response plan was opened, but its Montenegrin-language passages were not reliably translated for claims and were excluded.
Water-use conflict is a conditional planning warning, not evidence of observed intercommunal or armed violence. No source-stated conflict-to-adaptation pathway was verified.
Local social vulnerability and municipal capacity findings do not quantify municipality-specific exposure for Roma/Egyptian communities, women or persons with disabilities.
Drought governance recommendations date to 2020; municipal preparedness findings date to 2024. Their implementation and 2026 service readiness were not independently verified.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
